### Reliability and Validity

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
### `r fontawesome::fa("rotate", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Reliability

**Consistency of results if repeated under the same conditions.**

- Would you get similar results if repeated?
- Are measurements consistent?
- Is your procedure standardized?
]
]

.pull-right[
```{r img3, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="80%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/03-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

<br>

### Improving Reliability

.font90[
.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("list-check", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Standardize Procedures**

Use the same methods, instructions, and conditions for all participants or trials.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("wrench", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Check Instruments**

Ensure measuring tools are working properly and giving consistent readings.
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("rotate", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Multiple Trials**

Repeat measurements or tests to see if results are consistent.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("users", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Larger Sample Size**

Include more participants or items to reduce the impact of individual variations.
]
]
]

---
### Reliability and Validity

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
### `r fontawesome::fa("rotate", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Reliability

**Consistency of results if repeated under the same conditions.**
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-green[
### `r fontawesome::fa("bullseye", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Validity

**Whether you're actually measuring what you intend to measure.**

- Does your method truly address your question?
- Are your measurements relevant?
- Can you draw appropriate conclusions?
]
]

<div style="clear: both;"></div>

.center[.font110[Good research needs **both reliability and validity** to be trustworthy.]]

---
### Improving Validity

.pull-left[
```{r img5, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=4, fig.height=6, out.width="58%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/05-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

.pull-right[.font90[
<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">1</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Align Methods with Questions</strong><br>
  Choose research approaches that directly address what you want to know.</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">2</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Use Multiple Measures</strong><br>
  Collect different types of data to get a more complete picture of what you're studying.</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">3</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Control Variables</strong><br>
  Identify and minimize factors that could confuse your results.</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">4</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Pilot Test</strong><br>
  Try out your methods on a small scale first to identify and fix problems.</div>
</div>
]]

---
### Aisha's Research Revisited

.pull-left[
.content-box-yellow[
**`r fontawesome::fa("xmark", fill = "#D55E00")` Initial Approach (Poor)**

- Different music for each friend
- "Productivity" measured by self-reports of "fine" or "good"
- Different tasks for each person
- Inconsistent reporting methods
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("check", fill = "#009E73")` Improved Approach (Better)**

- Same calm music playlist for all
- Productivity measured by task completion and quiz scores
- Same reading and math tasks for everyone
- Consistent 30-minute sessions
]
]

<div style="clear: both;"></div>

.center[The improved design has **better reliability and validity**, leading to more trustworthy results.]

---
### Sampling: Who or What Will You Study?

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", fill = "#4a7fb5")` What is a Sample?**

A smaller subset of the population or items you're interested in.

Since studying everyone or everything is usually impossible, researchers select representatives.
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-yellow[
**`r fontawesome::fa("key", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Key Sampling Questions**

- How many people/items will you include?
- How will you select them?
- Will your sample represent the larger group?
- What potential biases might affect your selection?
]
]

<div style="clear: both;"></div>

.center[Good sampling makes your results more **reliable, generalizable and valid**.]

---
### Types of Sampling

.pull-left[.font90[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("dice", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Random Sampling**

Everyone has equal chance of selection (like drawing names from a hat).
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("layer-group", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Stratified Sampling**

Select from important subgroups to ensure representation (e.g., different grades).
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("object-group", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Cluster Sampling**

Randomly select entire groups (randomly choose 3 classrooms).
]
]]

--

.pull-right[.font90[
.content-box-yellow[
**`r fontawesome::fa("hand-point-right", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Convenience Sampling**

Select whoever is easiest to reach (like your own class).
]

.content-box-yellow[
**`r fontawesome::fa("bullseye", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Purposive Sampling**

Deliberately select specific cases based on research needs.
]
]]

---
### Sampling Examples

.pull-left[
```{r img8, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=4, fig.height=6, out.width="58%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/08-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

.pull-right[.font90[
#### `r fontawesome::fa("clipboard-list", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Survey
Instead of surveying all 1,200 students in a school, randomly select 120 students across all grade levels.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("seedling", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Plant Experiment
Use 30 plants of the same species and size, randomly assigning 15 to experimental and 15 to control groups.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("eye", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Observation
Instead of observing a park 24/7, sample time periods by observing for 1 hour on mornings and 1 hour on afternoons.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("landmark", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Historical Research
Instead of reading every newspaper from 100 years, sample by examining the first issue of each month from selected years.
]]

---
### Sampling Bias

.pull-left[
.content-box-yellow[
**`r fontawesome::fa("triangle-exclamation", fill = "#4a7fb5")` What is Sampling Bias?**

When your sample doesn't fairly represent the population you're studying.

This can skew results and lead to incorrect conclusions.
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("utensils", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Example**

Surveying only cooking club members about school lunch preferences would give biased results.

These students likely have different food interests than the general student body.
]
]

<div style="clear: both;"></div>

.center[Even with limited resources, try to **broaden your sample** to reduce obvious biases.]

### Practical Sampling Tips

.font90[
.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("tower-broadcast", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Broaden Your Reach**

Instead of just surveying friends, include students from different classes or groups.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("dice", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Use Random Selection**

When possible, use methods like drawing names or random number generators to select participants.
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("scale-balanced", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Consider Balance**

Try to include representation from important subgroups (different grades, genders, etc.).
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("comment-dots", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Acknowledge Limitations**

Be transparent about who your sample represents and any potential biases.
]
]
]

### Equipment Planning

.font90[
.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("laptop", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Technology**

Computers, tablets, cameras, recording devices, or specialized equipment.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("flask", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Lab Supplies**

Chemicals, test tubes, measuring tools, or experiment-specific materials.
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("file-lines", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Documentation Tools**

Survey forms, observation checklists, interview guides, or data collection sheets.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("ruler", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Measurement Instruments**

Stopwatches, rulers, scales, thermometers, or other measuring devices.
]
]
]

]]

### Access and Permissions

.font90[
.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("door-open", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Physical Spaces**

Permission to use classrooms, labs, libraries, or community spaces for your research.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("database", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Information Access**

Approval to use school records, databases, or other information sources.
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("signature", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Participant Consent**

Permission from people (and parents for minors) to participate in your study.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("building-columns", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Institutional Approval**

Permission from school administration for activities that affect school operations.
]
]
]

### People Resources

.pull-left[

]

.pull-right[.font90[
#### `r fontawesome::fa("people-group", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Research Team
Friends or classmates who will help conduct the research. List specific roles and responsibilities.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("user-check", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Participants
How many people will be in your study? How will you recruit them? What will they need to do?

#### `r fontawesome::fa("chalkboard-user", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Supervisors
Teachers, parents, or other adults who need to oversee activities, especially for safety or access reasons.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("user-graduate", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Experts
People with specialized knowledge who might advise on your project or help interpret results.
]]

### Timeline and Logistics

.font110[Your project moves through four phases:]

.font90[
<div class="chev-flow">
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("pen-ruler", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>1. Planning Phase</strong><br>
    Design research, create materials, get permissions, and prepare resources.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("table-list", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>2. Data Collection</strong><br>
    Conduct experiments, distribute surveys, perform interviews or observations.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("chart-line", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>3. Analysis</strong><br>
    Organize data, perform calculations, identify patterns, and interpret findings.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("share-nodes", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>4. Reporting</strong><br>
    Write up results, create visuals, prepare presentation, and share conclusions.</p>
  </div>
</div>
]

---
### Creating a Detailed Timeline

.pull-left[
```{r img17, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=4, fig.height=6, out.width="58%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/17-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

.pull-right[.font90[
<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">1</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Schedule Data Collection</strong><br>
  Plan exactly when you'll collect data, with specific dates and times.</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">2</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Estimate Duration</strong><br>
  Calculate how long each session or step will take to ensure it's feasible.</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">3</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Include Waiting Periods</strong><br>
  Account for necessary delays between steps, like plant growth or survey response time.</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">4</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Set Internal Deadlines</strong><br>
  Create target dates for completing each phase to stay on track throughout the project.</div>
</div>
]]

---
### Flexibility and Troubleshooting

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("triangle-exclamation", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Anticipate Challenges**

Think ahead about what might go wrong and how you'll handle it.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("arrows-rotate", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Be Ready to Adapt**

Prepare to adjust your methods if you discover better approaches.
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("file-pen", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Document Changes**

Record any modifications to your original plan and why you made them.
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("shield-halved", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Have Backup Plans**

Create alternative approaches for critical parts of your research.
]
]

class: segue-green

# NEXT: LITERATURE REVIEW `r top_icon("book-open")`

---
### What is a Literature Review?

.pull-left[
```{r img18, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=4, fig.height=6, out.width="58%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/18-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-blue[
A literature review is a **summary and analysis** of what has already been written on a topic.
]

**It helps you:**

#### `r fontawesome::fa("book-open", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Understand what's already known

#### `r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; See where there are gaps or debates

#### `r fontawesome::fa("ban", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Avoid repeating others' work

#### `r fontawesome::fa("trowel-bricks", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Build a strong foundation for your own research
]

---
### How to Conduct a Lit Review (Steps 1&ndash;4)

.font90[
<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">1</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Clarify Your Topic or Research Question</strong></div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">2</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Search for Reliable Sources</strong></div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">3</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Skim and Select</strong><br>
  Read abstracts first to decide if the source is relevant. Choose a mix of recent, relevant, and diverse perspectives. Aim for at least 5&ndash;10 solid sources (depending on assignment length).</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">4</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Take Notes</strong><br>
  Write down the main point of each source. Note how it relates to your topic, and any key quotes or data. Use color coding or a chart to organize themes or arguments.</div>
</div>
]

---
### How to Conduct a Lit Review (Steps 5&ndash;7)

.font90[
<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">5</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Group by Themes or Ideas</strong><br>
  Don't stop at summarizing each article one by one. Instead, group your notes by common themes, disagreements, or trends. Ask: What do these sources have in common? How do they differ?</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">6</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Start Writing</strong></div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev">7</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Cite Everything</strong></div>
</div>
]

---
### Literature Review Template (Short Version)

.pull-left[
```{r img18b, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=4, fig.height=6, out.width="58%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/18-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("flag", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Begin with a short introduction**

What is your topic? Why is it important?
]

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("paragraph", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Body**

Share what other studies have found. Organize the body **by themes, not by author**.
]

.content-box-green[
**`r fontawesome::fa("flag-checkered", fill = "#4a7fb5")` End with a summary**

Clarify how your project connects to past research.
]
]

---
### Importance of Giving Reference, aka Citing

.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("quote-right", fill = "#4a7fb5")` What is Citing?**

Citing your sources means **giving credit** to the original authors of the ideas, words, or data you use in your work.
]

--

**We cite to:**

#### `r fontawesome::fa("user-shield", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Avoid plagiarism (taking credit for someone else's work)

#### `r fontawesome::fa("map-pin", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Show where your information came from

#### `r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Help others find those sources if they want to learn more

---
### What to Cite? What Not to Cite?

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("check", fill = "#009E73")` You should cite:**

- Direct quotes (even short ones)
- Paraphrased ideas (putting someone else's idea into your own words)
- Statistics or data
- Images, charts, or graphics you didn't create
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-yellow[
**`r fontawesome::fa("xmark", fill = "#D55E00")` You do not need to cite:**

- Common knowledge (e.g., "Water freezes at 0&deg;C")
- Your own original thoughts
]
]

<div style="clear: both;"></div>

.font90[**How to cite** *(more about this on Day 8)*: name of the first author &amp; date&mdash;in the text; full info&mdash;on the references page.]

---
class: segue-yellow

# EXTRA SLIDES FOR DAY 5

---
### Common Research Challenges

.font80[
.three-col[
.col[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("user-slash", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Participation Issues**

- Low survey response rates
- Participants dropping out
- Scheduling conflicts

**Solution:** Recruit more than needed, send reminders, offer incentives, be flexible with scheduling.
]
]
.col[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("ruler", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Measurement Problems**

- Unclear results
- Equipment failures
- Inconsistent data

**Solution:** Test instruments beforehand, use multiple measures, document anomalies, increase sample size.
]
]
.col[
.content-box-blue[
**`r fontawesome::fa("coins", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Resource Limitations**

- Budget constraints
- Limited access
- Time shortages

**Solution:** Scale project appropriately, find alternatives, prioritize essential elements.
]
]
]
]

---
### Ethical Considerations

.pull-left[
```{r img21, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=4, fig.height=6, out.width="58%", fig.show='hold', fig.align='center'}
# Read the image file
img <- readPNG("assets/21-img.png")

# Plot the image
grid.raster(img)
```
]

.pull-right[.font80[
#### `r fontawesome::fa("user-shield", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Respect Privacy
Protect participants' identities and personal information. Use anonymous responses when possible.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("signature", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Informed Consent
Ensure participants understand what they're agreeing to. Get permission from parents for minors.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("heart", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Minimize Harm
Design research that doesn't cause physical or emotional distress to participants.

#### `r fontawesome::fa("stamp", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` &nbsp; Get Approvals
Obtain necessary permissions from teachers, administrators, or other authorities.
]]
